ssc.title: Curriculum Module: Subject Selection Teacher Counselling Guide 26-27

aia.title: Digital Citizenship & AI Appendix A: Academic Integrity Policy 26-27

essentials.title: Keep your lesson plans and class records up to date
essentials.description: These records are your F1 Teacher Administration evidence: lesson plans submitted on time, a current lesson journal, an accurate Gradebook and attendance recorded in every lesson. Keep them current as you go, not just before a visit.

source.quote: The teacher’s administrative documents: academic calendar knowledge, annual plan and syllabus, lesson plans, records and reporting.

essentials.title: Mark, give feedback and enter results within 5 working days
essentials.description: Students should get clear written feedback on how to improve within 5 working days, and results go into Edunav in the same time. Log major homework and project deadlines in the shared homework calendar so students are not overloaded.
essentials.timing_text: Within 5 working days of each assessment

source.quote: Enter all school/classroom assessment results within 5 working days of assessment completion

essentials.title: Re-teach, then reassess students who scored below KKTP
essentials.description: When a student scores below your school's KKTP on a Common Assessment, re-teach the topics they missed first, then give one short, targeted reassessment. Record the reteaching, the date and both scores in Edunav; a pass is entered at the KKTP value.
essentials.timing_text: Within 10 working days of each Common Assessment result

source.quote: Give one short reassessment — within 10 working days of the result.

essentials.title: Take part in your department meeting
essentials.description: Come ready to talk about coverage, student learning gaps, upcoming Teacher-Paced or Synchronized Test duties, homework load and one teaching idea. Every meeting ends with named actions, owners and due dates.
essentials.timing_text: Every two weeks — tick it in the weeks your department meets

source.quote: Departments meet at least every two weeks, with minutes and named actions

essentials.title: Prepare for each formal observation and act on the feedback
essentials.description: Your school's own appraisers observe you at least three times a semester, and only these observations count for F2. Teach as usual, send your plan in advance, then work on the agreed Glow / Grow / Go next step. Walkthroughs are developmental and never change your F2 score.
essentials.timing_text: Before and after each formal observation

source.quote: Please submit your lesson plan as a PDF via email, instant messaging, or through the school coordinator before the lesson observation

tasks.title: Check the Annual Plan and EASE Schedule for your classes
tasks.description: Note which chapters each Teacher-Paced Test covers and roughly when, the two EASE Weeks this semester and your school's report dates. Plan your teaching so each class reaches each checkpoint on time.
tasks.timing_text: First week of each semester

source.quote: Teacher-Paced Test checkpoints are set centrally in the Annual Plan — check your school's schedule for exact dates.

tasks.title: Do your self-review and agree your objectives for the year
tasks.description: Reflect on last year's successes, challenges and progress. Then agree this year's objectives with your appraiser, and the evidence (including classroom observation) that will show progress. Ask for support as soon as you need it.
tasks.timing_text: Start of the academic year

source.quote: Think about possible future objectives and training and development needs

tasks.title: Read your Student Survey result and plan one change
tasks.description: Students complete the survey at the end of each semester, without you present. Read your result in Edunav and write a short action plan for what you will do differently in your lessons.
tasks.timing_text: Once a semester, when the previous semester's result is in Edunav

source.quote: through their account in Edunav Appraisal platform and each teacher needs to create action plans accordingly.

tasks.title: State the permitted AI level on every task you set
tasks.description: If a task states no AI level, NO AI is the default for submitted work. Remind your classes what the academic integrity rules mean in your subject and how students must disclose AI use.
tasks.timing_text: On every task — suggested reminder to classes at the start of each semester

source.quote: Teachers must state the permitted AI level on every task.

tasks.title: Request Latihan.id time slots for this month's tests
tasks.description: For each Teacher-Paced Test, choose a regular lesson inside the window for each class and wait for the Grade Coordinator's approval. If a student is absent, mark them Excused and reopen the test for them later.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: start of each month (test windows follow the EASE Schedule)

source.quote: Teachers will need to request a time slot for each class to conduct the exams.

tasks.title: Get your classes ready for the EASE Growth week
tasks.description: EASE Growth needs no study and is not graded, so ask students simply to do their honest best. The Teacher-Paced Test that week covers only the latest chapters, and normal lessons continue.
tasks.timing_text: The week before EASE Week 1 (28 Sep–2 Oct 2026) and EASE Week 3 (29 Mar–2 Apr 2027)

source.quote: hosts the EASE Growth sitting (first two class periods) and a Teacher-Paced Test checkpoint, which covers only the most recent chapters

tasks.title: Prepare students for the Synchronized Test week
tasks.description: Students revise all of the semester's chapters; the test is online through Latihan.id, on the same day across the network. Afterwards, mark structured answers with the M1 / A1 / B1 mark scheme and enter results in Edunav before the end-of-semester reports.
tasks.timing_text: Last teaching week before EASE Week 2 (7–11 Dec 2026) and EASE Week 4 (10–14 May 2027)

source.quote: which is a Synchronized Test covering all chapters of the semester, with no lessons running during that exam week

tasks.title: Complete Gradebook entries and comments before midterm reports
tasks.description: Check every result is in Edunav under the right category, with comments on the major assessments. Parents see the Gradebook and the Report Score Prediction, so accuracy matters.
tasks.timing_text: Before the Mid-Term Progress Reports (17 October 2026 and 17 April 2027 in the network calendar)

source.quote: Add descriptive comments for major assessments (Common Assessment — Teacher-Paced and Synchronized Tests — Projects

tasks.title: Guide students to choose this semester's portfolio evidence
tasks.description: Aim for about 1–2 purposeful pieces per subject per semester, taken from normal work. Help students explain why each piece matters and what they will improve next. The portfolio is never graded.
tasks.applies_when: Your school runs the Grade 7–12 student portfolio for the classes you teach
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: mid-semester, ahead of your school's Student-Led Conference

source.quote: Supports selection of meaningful subject evidence and guides reflection. The teacher does not re-mark work simply because it enters the portfolio.

tasks.title: Help students prepare to lead their Student-Led Conference
tasks.description: Help each student pick a manageable amount of evidence, practise reflection language and set a realistic goal. On the day you facilitate, not present; move any serious concern to a private adult meeting.
tasks.applies_when: Your school runs the Grade 7–12 student portfolio for the classes you teach
tasks.timing_text: Before your school's SLC date (normally in the December and May final-report windows)

source.quote: Explain that the student, not the teacher, leads the meeting.

tasks.title: Talk through EASE Growth results with your students
tasks.description: Use the approved student-level information to discuss reasoning and reading strengths and support needs. In 2026-27 it is a baseline: never call a result growth and never grade it.
tasks.timing_text: When your school releases the student-level information (suggested placement; release follows Eduversal's data checks)

source.quote: Teachers then receive approved student-level information for discussion with students

tasks.title: Add this semester's evidence to your F3 file
tasks.description: F3 covers punctuality, task completion, PD, co-curricular work, collegial work and communication with parents. Save evidence as it happens so you do not rebuild it in May.
tasks.timing_text: Suggested: end of Semester I (keep adding evidence all year)

source.quote: Evidence is gathered throughout the year and presented by the teacher at the End-of-Year Conference.

tasks.title: Prepare for your End-of-Year Conference
tasks.description: Bring your F3 evidence: the conference adds F3 to your year of F2 observations, F1 and Student Survey and finalises your record. When your final scores are in Edunav, draft one professional goal for next year.
tasks.timing_text: Later in Semester II, before your conference date

source.quote: The End-of-Year Conference session, held later in Semester 2, retrieves the accumulated appraisal record

tasks.title: Start preparing for EASE Academic
tasks.description: Read the Tier 1 resources about one a fortnight, review your syllabus objectives and command words about four weeks out, and read the latest Principal Examiner Report the week before.
tasks.applies_when: You teach English, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology or Integrated Science
tasks.timing_text: About 8 weeks before each EASE Academic date (5 Dec 2026, 15 May 2027)

source.quote: Read the Tier 1 resources, one per fortnight. Approximately one hour each.

tasks.title: Sit the EASE Academic exam
tasks.description: 50 questions in 120 minutes on Latihan.id. Your score is shared only with you and is used for professional development only. If you cannot attend, tell your principal and the Academic Board before the exam date.
tasks.applies_when: You teach English, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology or Integrated Science
tasks.timing_text: Once a semester: 5 December 2026 and 15 May 2027

source.quote: All teachers currently teaching Grades 1–12 in English, Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and Integrated Science.

tasks.title: Give and mark the Cambridge Progression Test
tasks.description: Use it once the stage is mostly taught: Stage 8 around September–October, Stage 7 around January, Stage 9 about 4–6 weeks before Checkpoint. Record results as non-weighted evidence and use them to plan re-teaching.
tasks.applies_when: You teach Lower Secondary English, English as a Second Language, Mathematics or Science (Stage 9 is required for Checkpoint schools; Stages 7 and 8 are recommended)
tasks.timing_text: When each stage is complete (suggested placement; follow your subject's Annual Plan)

source.quote: Subject teachers administer and mark the tests using the current Cambridge mark scheme and guidance.

tasks.title: Advise students on their readiness for your subject
tasks.description: Explain what the subject really involves, review the evidence and say clearly and early if a prerequisite is missing. Record the reason in the Student Subject Counselling Record; the Academic Coordinator owns the final decision.
tasks.applies_when: You teach Grade 8 or Grade 10 students choosing IGCSE or AS Level subjects
tasks.timing_text: Semester II counselling window (suggested placement)

source.quote: A subject teacher advises on readiness for the subject.

tasks.title: Meet your mentor and answer the Friday pulse
tasks.description: Contact eases over time: daily for 15 minutes in your first three weeks, weekly for an hour in Semester 1, weekly for 30 minutes in Semester 2 and monthly in Semester 3. Nothing from induction feeds your appraisal.
tasks.applies_when: You are in Teacher Induction (your first three semesters)
tasks.timing_text: Every week (monthly mentor contact in Semester 3)

source.quote: Weekly pulse (every Friday): one question, "How was your week?", on a 5-emoji scale.

tasks.title: Have this month's mentor observation and debrief
tasks.description: Your mentor observes for 30–45 minutes and debriefs the same day. The focus moves month by month: routines, objectives, questioning, differentiation, assessment for learning, engagement, pacing, then your own challenge area.
tasks.applies_when: You are in your first year of Teacher Induction
tasks.timing_text: Once a month, August to March (Months 2–9)

source.quote: The Observation Spine — one mentor observation every month (Months 2–9).

tasks.title: Join your mini lesson-study cycle
tasks.description: With your mentor and one or two subject colleagues, plan one lesson together, teach it while the group observes, then reflect on the lesson itself. Nothing from it is scored.
tasks.applies_when: You are in your first year of Teacher Induction
tasks.timing_text: Once per semester (suggested: mid-semester)

source.quote: Once per semester (Semester 1 and Semester 2), you join a small planning group

tasks.title: Prepare for your Integration Checkpoint
tasks.description: Agree the focus with your school leader, who observes one full lesson. With your mentor, write a mid-programme reflection and a Semester 3 focus plan. The checkpoint is developmental and stays inside induction.
tasks.applies_when: You are in your first year of Teacher Induction
tasks.timing_text: End of Semester 2; the observed lesson is no later than 7 May 2027

source.quote: Integration Checkpoint with your school leader (the observed lesson takes place no later than the last teaching day, 7 May 2027)

tasks.title: Prepare for your Final Induction Completion Review
tasks.description: Write a one-page reflection on your 18 months and a post-induction development plan, which your mentor reviews. Your school leader then observes a lesson and signs off your induction.
tasks.applies_when: You are in your third induction semester (Year 2, Semester I)
tasks.timing_text: End of Semester 3

source.quote: Your post-induction professional development plan: which competency areas you want to deepen next

tasks.title: Hold your weekly mentor session
tasks.description: Use the standard structure: check-in, review last week's action, preview next week, one curriculum or pedagogy topic, and one or two actions with an owner and date. A group workshop does not replace it.
tasks.applies_when: You are a certified mentor with an active mentee
tasks.timing_text: Every week (30 minutes in Semester 2; monthly in Semester 3)

source.quote: Standard rhythm: weekly one-hour mentor session plus the Observation Spine and agreed practice tasks.

tasks.title: Observe your mentee and debrief the same day
tasks.description: Write low-inference evidence, hold a 10–15 minute debrief that starts with the mentee's own reflection, and agree one Glow, one Grow and one Go. Write it up within 7 days; it never enters appraisal.
tasks.applies_when: You are a certified mentor with a first-year mentee
tasks.timing_text: Once a month, August to March (Months 2–9)

source.quote: Stage 2 is on track when weekly mentoring is happening, early plans show increased independence, monthly observations and debriefs are current

tasks.title: Map your mentee's 8-touch cycle for Semester 2
tasks.description: Plan the two co-teaches, four mentor observations and two peer observations as one schedule, so no formal observation is duplicated just to satisfy two labels.
tasks.applies_when: You are a certified mentor with a first-year mentee
tasks.timing_text: Start of Semester 2

source.quote: At the beginning of Semester 2, map all eight touches against the school calendar and the Month 7–9 observation requirements.

tasks.title: Attend the mentor Calibration Session
tasks.description: All active mentors score the same anonymised sample observation and compare results, so the Emerging → Extending scale means the same thing in every school.
tasks.applies_when: You are a certified mentor with an active mentee
tasks.timing_text: Once per semester, on the date Eduversal sets (suggested placement)

source.quote: all active mentors attend a Calibration Session once per semester (90 minutes, online)

notes_for_reviewer: v1 problems found (subject-teacher.json v1.1): (1) a 40-week arc (W1–W40, Semester II from W19) instead of 36 teaching weeks, so EASE Week 1 sat at W10, the Synchronized Tests at W14/W16 and W33 and the End-of-Year Conference at W39 — in reality EASE Weeks 2 and 4 fall after the last teaching week (7–11 Dec, 10–14 May) and the appraisal year must finish by 7 May; (2) a 'compliance' priority on about 20 tasks, backed by Indonesian regulatory anchors no live document uses (Permendikbud 6/2018 is about teachers assigned as principals; the 37.5-hour workload rule); (3) tasks with no live basis — learn every student's name in Week 1, a Week 2 baseline diagnostic, fixed-week report comments, archiving and handover notes, 'reset routines' in W19; (4) another role's duty — checking Cambridge entries with the Exams Officer (Exams Officer / Cambridge Coordinator process); (5) citations to documents that are not in the school-facing export (Teaching & Learning: Learning Environment 26-27, Lesson Planning Guide & Template 26-27) and the old name 'Teacher Capacity Building Guide'; (6) the Capacity-Building Guide's two coaching touches a semester turned into a weekly 'try your growth-focus strategy' task, and the induction overlay mixed into the main list without a condition.

New optional field `applies_when` (a plain sentence) is used on 15 of 26 tasks: the student portfolio / SLC (ST2-014/015), EASE Academic subjects (ST2-019/020), Lower Secondary Progression Tests (ST2-021), subject counselling (ST2-022), Teacher Induction (ST2-023 to ST2-027) and mentors (ST2-028 to ST2-031). The seeder and the Teachers Hub page need to support it (an 'Only if…' line, or a filter on the user's induction / mentor status). Without it, every teacher would see mentor and mentee tasks every week.

Lesson planning and classroom routines: Teaching & Learning: Lesson Planning Guide & Template 26-27, Learning Environment 26-27 and Classroom Management 26-27 are cited across the live pack but are NOT in the as-export folder, so no task could quote them. ST2-001 rests on Teacher Appraisal F1 instead. Please check whether these documents exist in Drive and should be exported; a planning-routine task could then quote them directly.

Calendar conflicts (live document used): the Assessment Policy §8.4 gives the Semester II Mid-Term Progress Reports as 17 March 2027 (calendar-2026-27.txt: 17 April) — ST2-013 uses 17 March; the AC file uses the April date (AC2-026), so the two files disagree until this is settled. The same section gives the Semester I start as 15 July 2026 (calendar: teaching from 13 July) and semester-end assessment blocks of 7–18 December and 10–28 May (calendar: EASE Exam, then Leadership Camp).

Student-Led Conferences: the Assessment Policy §8.4 says the portfolio-led SLC 'normally falls in the December final-report/parent-conference window' (May for Semester II), i.e. after the last teaching week. ST2-015 is therefore one week before each semester ends; ST2-014 (evidence selection) sits mid-semester.

EASE timing: EASE Weeks 1 and 3 are skipped weeks in the seeder calendar although lessons continue, so ST2-011 shows in the teaching week before them (21 Sep 2026, 22 Mar 2027) without lead_weeks. EASE Academic (Saturday 5 Dec 2026 and 15 May 2027) falls back to the weeks of 30 Nov and 3 May. Release dates for student-level EASE Growth information are not in the live documents; ST2-016 (2 Nov 2026, 26 Apr 2027) is a suggested placement.

Student Survey (ST2-008): results reach Edunav after each semester. The Semester I placement reads the previous year's Semester 2 result; the Semester II placement reads the Semester 1 result. The 2026-27 Semester 2 result arrives after the teaching weeks and rolls into next year's first placement.

Progression Tests (ST2-021): the Assessment Policy gives Stage 8 'around September–October', Stage 7 'January' when Stage 7 finishes by December, and Stage 9 '4–6 weeks before' Checkpoint. 21 Sep, 11 Jan and 15 Mar are placements, not live dates; the Checkpoint date sits in Quality Ecosystem: External Exams & Admissions 26-27. The subject leader file spot-checks the marking one or two weeks later (SL2-023).

Title drift to confirm against Drive: (a) 'Teacher Appraisal: Pre-Observation Information' has no '26-27' in its footer; (b) the counselling guide's header says 'Subject Selection Teacher Counselling Guide 26-27' and its footer 'Curriculum Module: Subject Selection Counselling 26-27' — I used the export file name 'Curriculum Module: Subject Selection Teacher Counselling Guide 26-27'; (c) 'Career Growth: Framework 26-27' is not used in this file (the department-meeting rhythm is quoted from the Department Handbook Template instead).

Deliberately not made teacher tasks: the school-wide baseline assessment week (Assessment Policy §2.1a does not say who administers it), unit diagnostics (every unit, no calendar placement — could be added to ST2-001's description), parent-teacher conferences (dates set by each school; the Parent-Teacher Conference Guide is a how-to), Cambridge entries, invigilation and predicted grades (Exams Officer / Cambridge Coordinator processes), EASE Growth invigilation details (the Principal's Guide gives readiness to the school), and the Weekly Teacher Tool Share Tracker (explicitly optional).

Load, simulated with my own reading of the `when` rules over 36 teaching weeks (semester_mid = week floor(n/2), i.e. 21 Sep and 8 Mar; monthly = by the Monday's month): a typical teacher (no applies_when tasks) has 0–2 dated tasks a week plus the 5 essentials. Realistic heavier cases stay within 5: a first-year induction teacher in Lower Secondary peaks at 5 (week of 21 Sep 2026); a mentor peaks at 5 (weeks of 21 Sep 2026 and 4 Jan 2027). The theoretical maximum with every applies_when task on (mentor and mentee at once) is 7. Please re-run with the real seeder.
2026-10-02 review: ST2-013 aligned with the network calendar (Semester II mid-term reports 17 April 2027, as AC2-026); the Assessment Policy §8.4 says 17 March 2027 — conflict raised with Alif.

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: Set up and rehearse classroom routines in the first two weeks of the year (entry, transitions, getting attention).
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The most-cited first-weeks habit in the induction material, but no live document gives every teacher a start-of-year routine task; it would also anchor F2 Domain 2.

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: Learn every student's name in the first week, using a seating plan with photos.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: A low-cost relationship habit that supports F3.8 (student dignity) and classroom climate; currently only implied.

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: Write the semester report comments for every student before the end-of-semester report date.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The Assessment Policy fixes the report dates (19 Dec, 29 May) but gives teachers no deadline or quality standard for report comments.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Curriculum Module: Assessment Policy 26-27 (§8.4 Reporting Schedule)

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: Check with the Exams Officer that your Cambridge candidates are entered for the right syllabus, tier and components.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: Wrong tier or component entries are costly and the subject teacher is the person most likely to notice; the Exams Officer Handbook names subject teachers only for post-results services.

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: Prepare handover notes when a class moves to a new teacher (cohort strengths, concerns, students needing continued support).
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The Department Handbook Template has a handover routine for Subject Leaders but not for class teachers, so student-support continuity is lost each July.

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: A short journal-entry rhythm for teachers in induction (for example a few sentences each week).
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The journal is protected by NN2 and the first entry is set for Day 3, but no live text says how often to write after that.
